record.paper_title: Distinct Distances: Open Problems and Current Bounds
record.original_question: Let subset_prime(n) be the largest integer such that every n-point set in the plane contains a subset of size subset_prime(n) that spans no isosceles triangle. Determine the asymptotic order of subset_prime(n).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For a finite set $P$ of points in the Euclidean plane $\mathbb{R}^2$, say that $P$ spans an isosceles triangle if there exist three distinct points $a,b,c \in P$ (not all collinear) such that at least two of the three Euclidean distances $|ab|$, $|bc|$, $|ca|$ are equal. Define
$$\mathrm{subset}'(n) \;=\; \min_{\substack{P \subset \mathbb{R}^2 \\ |P| = n}} \; \max\bigl\{\, |Q| : Q \subseteq P \text{ and } Q \text{ spans no isosceles triangle}\,\bigr\}.$$
In other words, $\mathrm{subset}'(n)$ is the largest integer $m$ such that every $n$-point set in the plane contains an $m$-point subset no three of whose points form an isosceles triangle. Determine the asymptotic order of $\mathrm{subset}'(n)$ as $n \to \infty$.

Known partial bounds include the trivial upper bound $\mathrm{subset}'(n) = O(\sqrt{n}/(\log n)^{1/4})$ and a lower bound of the form $\mathrm{subset}'(n) = \Omega(n^{c})$ for some constant $c > 0$ (e.g. $c \approx 0.4315$). The task is to close the gap and determine the true asymptotic growth rate.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem of determining the asymptotic order of the largest isosceles-triangle-free subset guaranteed in any n-point planar set appears to remain open. Known results provide only a polynomial gap: a lower bound of roughly Ω(n^0.4315) (improving on Lefmann–Thiele's Ω(n^{1/4})) and an upper bound of O(√n/(log n)^{1/4}) inherited from distinct-distances bounds. No recent paper appears to determine the asymptotic order.

status_evidence.title: Isosceles Triangles Determined by a Planar Point Set
status_evidence.snippet: Lefmann and Thiele established the lower bound subset(n) = Ω(n^{1/4}) using a probabilistic argument; the corresponding upper bound is essentially the distinct-distances bound.
status_evidence.claim: Best known lower and upper bounds remain polynomially apart, indicating the asymptotic value is not determined.

status_evidence.title: The largest isosceles triangle-free subset of the grid (JMM 2025)
status_evidence.snippet: Recent work studies the largest isosceles-triangle-free subset of an N×N grid, indicating the general planar problem is still actively investigated.
status_evidence.claim: The problem is still being actively studied as of 2025, with no resolution of the asymptotic order.
